steps.headline: Tapping a chip in the editor opens it, so you can rewrite the prompt it sends instead of deleting the chip and building it again.
steps.changed: The row you tap expands into a name box and a full prompt box, with Save and Cancel. It uses the same two boxes the Add Chip form already uses. Both pictures show the same click: on the left it does nothing, on the right the row opens.
steps.measured: 3 steps to reword a prompt before (delete, re-add, drag back into place); 1 now
steps.notice: The prompt box is three lines tall, so you can read the whole prompt — the one-line preview in the closed row is clipped to about six words and always has been. A small pencil appears on a row when you point at it, so it is visible that rows can be opened. Dragging a row to reorder still works and does not open it; Escape closes the open row first, then the window.
steps.risk: The row you have open closes without saving if you delete or drag any chip while it is open — the app tracks chips by position, so a shifted position could otherwise write your edit onto the wrong chip.
